samples.summary: moveCells now recomputes the moved merge map *after* the `await store.moveCells(...)` instead of before it, so a remote change that lands during that await can make the remap run twice
samples.evidence: Before this delta `moveCells` captured `const movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, ...)` *before* `await this.store.moveCells(...)` and assigned it afterwards. The delta drops that capture and instead does `this.merges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst)` at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1624, i.e. after the await. The out-of-diff consumer that makes this matter is packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5230-5237 `reloadDimensions()` — documented "Call this when a remote change arrives" — which calls `sheet.loadMerges()` and replaces `this.merges` wholesale from the store (sheet.ts:590-592). `store.moveCells` in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:510-527 has already written the move into the CRDT, so a `loadMerges()` interleaved at that await point returns the *already moved* map; line 1624 then applies `moveMergeMap` to it a second time and the in-memory merge anchors end up at coordinates that match neither the document nor the render. The old ordering could not double-apply because it snapshotted the pre-move map. Fix belongs on the new code: capture the moved map before the await as before, or re-read/guard after it.

finding.summary: moveCells now recomputes the moved merge map *after* the `await store.moveCells(...)` instead of before it, so a remote change that lands during that await can make the remap run twice
finding.evidence: Before this delta `moveCells` captured `const movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, ...)` *before* `await this.store.moveCells(...)` and assigned it afterwards. The delta drops that capture and instead does `this.merges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst)` at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1624, i.e. after the await. The out-of-diff consumer that makes this matter is packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5230-5237 `reloadDimensions()` — documented "Call this when a remote change arrives" — which calls `sheet.loadMerges()` and replaces `this.merges` wholesale from the store (sheet.ts:590-592). `store.moveCells` in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:510-527 has already written the move into the CRDT, so a `loadMerges()` interleaved at that await point returns the *already moved* map; line 1624 then applies `moveMergeMap` to it a second time and the in-memory merge anchors end up at coordinates that match neither the document nor the render. verdict.reason: The cited code exists (sheet.ts:1593 await, sheet.ts:1624 post-await `moveMergeMap`), but the claimed interleaving is unreachable. (a) Every Store.moveCells in the repo has a fully synchronous body — YorkieStore (yorkie-store.ts:510-540, a sync doc.update/batchOps.push; the entire file has one `await`, line 272), MemStore (memory.ts:350-419), ReadOnlyStore (readonly.ts:150-157) — and these are the only three `implements Store` classes, so the await at sheet.ts:1593 yields only to the microtask queue; no frame/timer/network callback can run before line 1624. (b) The remote-change path that calls loadMerges is deferred through requestAnimationFrame: doc.subscribe -> scheduleRemoteSync (sheet-view.tsx:1322-1330) -> requestAnimationFrame (sheet-view.tsx:1201-1207) -> reloadDimensions (sheet-view.tsx:1183-1184 -> worksheet.ts:5230-5237). Even if a remote op lands while the CRDT write settles, the subscriber only schedules a frame callback. (c) A reload chain cannot already be parked at that boundary: reloadDimensions awaits only sheet loaders that await sync-bodied store getters (yorkie-store.ts:1068-1076, memory.ts:595-597), so it completes within a single microtask drain and cannot straddle the user-event macrotask that starts a move (worksheet.ts:4656-4659, pointer handler). (d) No aliasing double-apply: moveMergeMap returns a new map (merging.ts:367-382) and getMerges returns copies, so remapping the sheet's own copy after the write is equivalent to a pre-await capture.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present verbatim: sheet-view.tsx:1242-1244 passes `Object.entries(ws.merges ?? {})` into `buildMergeCoverMap`, where `ws` comes from the live Yorkie proxy (`root.sheets[targetTabId]` at :1233, `doc.getRoot()` at :1222). finding.summary: Cross-sheet formula resolver builds a merge cover map from the raw CRDT merge map, bypassing every clamp `rebuildMergeCoverMap` just gained
finding.evidence: `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:880-913) now spends `mergeBudgetAdmits`, try/catches `parseRef`, and rejects keys that do not round-trip through `toSref` — explicitly because anyone holding `rw` on the document can put an arbitrary merge map into the plain CRDT field. `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1235-1246` performs the *same* covered-cell walk over another tab's `ws.merges` read straight from `doc.getRoot()`: `Object.entries(ws.merges)` (not `safeWorksheetRecordEntries`, which the rest of that file uses for exactly the duplicate-key hazard), an unguarded `parseRef(anchorSref)`, and an unbounded `for r < anchorRef.r + span.rs / for c < ... + span.cs` nested loop. A single `{rs:1000000, cs:18278}` span — the case the new test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:66 asserts the engine now drops — freezes the tab here for 1.8e10 iterations, and a `__proto__`/`A1:B2` key throws out of the resolver, breaking every cross-sheet formula. The guard belongs on this site too (reuse `mergeBudgetAdmits` + `safeWorksheetRecordEntries`, or read the clamped map from `Sheet.getMerges()`).

verdict.reason: The cited site does not contain the code described. sheet-view.tsx:1242-1244 does not perform an inline covered-cell walk or call parseRef on merge keys; it calls the shared `buildMergeCoverMap` (imported at sheet-view.tsx:10), which is the identical function `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` delegates to (sheet.ts:877). All the clamps the finding says are bypassed live inside that shared reader: `isCountableMergeSpan` (merging.ts:179), `mergeBudgetAdmits` before the nested walk (merging.ts:180), try/catch around `parseRef` (merging.ts:183-190), and the `toSref` round-trip rejection (merging.ts:194). So the specific harms alleged are impossible here: the `{rs:1000000, cs:18278}` span from merge.test.ts:66 is refused by the budget check before any iteration, and a `__proto__` or `A1:B2` key is skipped rather than throwing. merging.ts:155-159 documents that the clamp was placed in the shared module precisely so this frontend resolver gets it. The only residual difference is `Object.entries` instead of `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` (worksheet-record.ts:47-61) — a distinct, narrower duplicate-own-keys concern, not a bypass of the new clamps, and the finding's supporting claim that "the rest of that file uses" the safe helper is also false (sheet-view.tsx never imports it; see plain Object.entries at 1278 and Object.values at 1160).
